The global Responsive Neurostimulation System market was valued at approximately USD 500 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 1.65 billion by 2034, expanding at a CAGR of 14.2% from 2026-2034. Market growth is supported by the rising prevalence of drug-resistant epilepsy, increased adoption of closed-loop neuromodulation, expanding clinical evidence, and continued development of personalized brain-stimulation technologies. Responsive neurostimulation combines implantable neurostimulators, intracranial leads, programming tools, data-management software, and cloud-based analytics. The technology supports continuous brain-activity monitoring and targeted stimulation based on detected seizure-related patterns. NeuroPace, Inc., developer of the FDA-approved RNS System, currently anchors the commercial market, while established and emerging neuromodulation companies compete through adjacent technologies. Responsive Neurostimulation System Market Highlights Drug-resistant focal epilepsy represented 88% of the market by indication in 2025. Implantable neurostimulators accounted for 62% of market revenue by component. Adults represented 84% of the market by age group. Hospitals and epilepsy centers held a 71% share by end user. North America generated 82% of global revenue in 2025. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing regional market through 2034. Key Responsive Neurostimulation System Market Growth Drivers The increasing burden of drug-resistant epilepsy remains the market's primary growth catalyst. A significant proportion of patients continue to experience seizures despite treatment with multiple antiseizure medications. For patients who are unsuitable for resective surgery, responsive neurostimulation provides an important therapeutic option supported by growing clinical adoption. The transition toward closed-loop, personalized neuromodulation is also accelerating demand. Responsive systems use recorded brain activity to guide stimulation, supporting greater therapeutic precision and individualized treatment. Advances in artificial intelligence, detection algorithms, cloud-based analytics, and remote monitoring are strengthening clinical decision-making and enabling more efficient long-term therapy management. Long-term clinical findings demonstrating durable seizure reduction are improving confidence among clinicians, patients, and payers. Growth opportunities are also emerging from potential indication expansion into idiopathic generalized epilepsy, adolescent focal epilepsy, and other neurological applications. Next-generation platforms featuring longer battery life, faster data transfer, improved recording capacity, and less invasive designs could further support adoption. Market Restraints High device, implantation, and follow-up costs continue to restrict access, particularly in markets with limited reimbursement. Treatment requires neurosurgical implantation, specialized epilepsy evaluation, seizure-focus localization, and long-term device programming. These capabilities are primarily available through comprehensive epilepsy centers, limiting adoption in regions with insufficient clinical infrastructure. Additional barriers include lengthy regulatory timelines, uneven reimbursement policies, limited physician and patient awareness, and competition from resective surgery, laser ablation, vagus nerve stimulation, and deep brain stimulation. Market concentration around one approved responsive neurostimulation platform also limits current product choice and commercial competition. Responsive Neurostimulation System Market Segment Analysis By Indication: Drug-resistant focal epilepsy accounted for approximately 88% of the market in 2025. Its leadership reflects established regulatory approval, more than a decade of clinical use, reimbursement availability, and a substantial long-term evidence base. Idiopathic generalized epilepsy represents a major emerging opportunity, particularly following positive clinical trial findings involving generalized tonic-clonic seizures. By Component: Implantable neurostimulators generated approximately 62% of 2025 revenue. These devices contain the detection, stimulation, recording, and power-management capabilities central to responsive therapy. Leads and accessories remain essential to each implantation, while software and services are expected to grow rapidly as AI-driven analytics, cloud platforms, and remote patient management become more widely integrated. By Age Group: Adults held an 84% market share in 2025, consistent with the approved patient population and current clinical practice. Adolescents and pediatric patients represent a potential growth segment as clinical research and regulatory programs evaluate broader age-based eligibility. By End User: Hospitals and epilepsy centers represented approximately 71% of the market. Their dominance is supported by access to multidisciplinary teams, intracranial monitoring, neurosurgical facilities, device programming, and long-term follow-up services. Specialty neurology clinics are expected to assume a larger role in programming and remote management, while ambulatory surgical centers may benefit from future procedural improvements. Regional Market Outlook North America accounted for 82% of global Responsive Neurostimulation System market revenue in 2025. Regional leadership is driven by FDA approval, established reimbursement, advanced healthcare infrastructure, high adoption of neurotechnology, and a dense network of comprehensive epilepsy centers. The United States remains the principal commercial market and the center of clinical trials, indication-expansion initiatives, and implant activity. Europe represents the leading market outside North America, with opportunities concentrated in Germany, the United Kingdom, France, and Nordic countries. Future growth will depend on regulatory authorization, reimbursement, and greater availability of specialist epilepsy services. Asia-Pacific is projected to record the fastest growth from a comparatively small base. China, Japan, India, South Korea, and Australia offer significant long-term potential due to large patient populations, rising healthcare investment, and expanding neurology and epilepsy-surgery infrastructure. Regulatory approval, affordability, specialist training, and reimbursement will remain critical to regional commercialization. Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa remain early-stage markets. Select private healthcare systems and specialist centers may provide initial adoption opportunities, although broader penetration requires stronger neurosurgical capacity and supportive funding frameworks. Competitive Landscape The Responsive Neurostimulation System market is highly consolidated, with NeuroPace, Inc. operating as the sole manufacturer of an FDA-approved brain-responsive neurostimulation platform. Its competitive position is reinforced by regulatory experience, intellectual property, chronic brain-recording capabilities, established clinical evidence, and an expanding data platform. Adjacent competitors include Medtronic plc, Boston Scientific Corporation, LivaNova PLC, Abbott Laboratories, Nevro Corp., Aleva Neurotherapeutics SA, Newronika S.p.A., Precisis GmbH, and Flow Neuroscience AB. These companies participate in deep brain stimulation, vagus nerve stimulation, adaptive stimulation, and other neuromodulation categories that may compete for eligible epilepsy patients or contribute to future responsive technologies. Competitive priorities include indication expansion, improved seizure-detection algorithms, longer battery performance, minimally invasive implantation, AI-driven analysis, remote monitoring, and integration of clinical data. High capital requirements, extensive clinical-evidence standards, regulatory complexity, and specialized intellectual property create substantial barriers to entry. Recent Responsive Neurostimulation System Market Developments In December 2025, NeuroPace filed a Premarket Approval Supplement with the FDA seeking an expanded RNS System indication for patients with antiseizure-medication-resistant idiopathic generalized epilepsy and generalized tonic-clonic seizures. In December 2025, NeuroPace reported positive preliminary 18-month NAUTILUS trial results, including a 77% median reduction in generalized tonic-clonic seizures. In 2026, three-year Post-Approval Study findings published in Neurology reported an 82% median seizure reduction in drug-resistant focal epilepsy among 324 implanted patients across 32 United States centers. Clinical validation, broader regulatory indications, improved reimbursement, and expansion of specialist treatment centers will determine the pace of adoption. Continued innovation in implantable hardware, AI-enabled analytics, cloud-based monitoring, and personalized stimulation is expected to strengthen the role of responsive neurostimulation within the global neuromodulation market. The global Responsive Neurostimulation System market was valued at approximately USD 500 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 1.65 billion by 2034, expanding at a CAGR of 14.2% from 2026-2034. Market growth is supported by the rising prevalence of drug-resistant epilepsy, increased adoption of closed-loop neuromodulation, expanding clinical evidence, and continued development of personalized brain-stimulation technologies.
Responsive neurostimulation combines implantable neurostimulators, intracranial leads, programming tools, data-management software, and cloud-based analytics. The technology supports continuous brain-activity monitoring and targeted stimulation based on detected seizure-related patterns. NeuroPace, Inc., developer of the FDA-approved RNS System, currently anchors the commercial market, while established and emerging neuromodulation companies compete through adjacent technologies.

Key Responsive Neurostimulation System Market Growth Drivers
The increasing burden of drug-resistant epilepsy remains the market's primary growth catalyst. A significant proportion of patients continue to experience seizures despite treatment with multiple antiseizure medications. For patients who are unsuitable for resective surgery, responsive neurostimulation provides an important therapeutic option supported by growing clinical adoption.
The transition toward closed-loop, personalized neuromodulation is also accelerating demand. Responsive systems use recorded brain activity to guide stimulation, supporting greater therapeutic precision and individualized treatment. Advances in artificial intelligence, detection algorithms, cloud-based analytics, and remote monitoring are strengthening clinical decision-making and enabling more efficient long-term therapy management.
Long-term clinical findings demonstrating durable seizure reduction are improving confidence among clinicians, patients, and payers. Growth opportunities are also emerging from potential indication expansion into idiopathic generalized epilepsy, adolescent focal epilepsy, and other neurological applications. Next-generation platforms featuring longer battery life, faster data transfer, improved recording capacity, and less invasive designs could further support adoption.
Market Restraints
High device, implantation, and follow-up costs continue to restrict access, particularly in markets with limited reimbursement. Treatment requires neurosurgical implantation, specialized epilepsy evaluation, seizure-focus localization, and long-term device programming. These capabilities are primarily available through comprehensive epilepsy centers, limiting adoption in regions with insufficient clinical infrastructure.
Additional barriers include lengthy regulatory timelines, uneven reimbursement policies, limited physician and patient awareness, and competition from resective surgery, laser ablation, vagus nerve stimulation, and deep brain stimulation. Market concentration around one approved responsive neurostimulation platform also limits current product choice and commercial competition.

Competitive Landscape
The Responsive Neurostimulation System market is highly consolidated, with NeuroPace, Inc. operating as the sole manufacturer of an FDA-approved brain-responsive neurostimulation platform. Its competitive position is reinforced by regulatory experience, intellectual property, chronic brain-recording capabilities, established clinical evidence, and an expanding data platform.
Adjacent competitors include Medtronic plc, Boston Scientific Corporation, LivaNova PLC, Abbott Laboratories, Nevro Corp., Aleva Neurotherapeutics SA, Newronika S.p.A., Precisis GmbH, and Flow Neuroscience AB. These companies participate in deep brain stimulation, vagus nerve stimulation, adaptive stimulation, and other neuromodulation categories that may compete for eligible epilepsy patients or contribute to future responsive technologies.
Competitive priorities include indication expansion, improved seizure-detection algorithms, longer battery performance, minimally invasive implantation, AI-driven analysis, remote monitoring, and integration of clinical data. High capital requirements, extensive clinical-evidence standards, regulatory complexity, and specialized intellectual property create substantial barriers to entry.

Accessibility: Skip TopNav NovaBridge Appoints Martin Dewhurst to Board of Directors as an Independent Director September 08, 2026 07:00 ET | Source: NovaBridge Biosciences NovaBridge Biosciences Martin Dewhurst appointed as independent director and member of the Audit and Compensation Committees Veteran healthcare executive brings more than 30 years of leadership, governance, and strategic advisory experience ROCKVILLE, Md., Sept.  08, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NovaBridge Biosciences (Nasdaq: NBP) (“NovaBridge” or the “Company”), a global biotechnology company that identifies differentiated innovation and applies disciplined development, financing, and partnering strategies to create value, today announced the appointment of Martin Dewhurst to its Board of Directors (the “Board”) as an independent director, and as a member of both the Audit Committee and the Compensation Committee, effective immediately. Mr. Dewhurst is a global healthcare leader with more than 30 years of Board and C-suite experience across biotech, biopharma, medical devices, health tech, and healthcare investment. He has served as a Board Director, Audit Committee Chair, Remuneration Committee member, and strategic advisor, with governance and operating experience spanning the United States, Europe, China, India, Africa and the Middle East. His expertise includes growth strategy, transformation, governance, investor engagement, and scaling businesses globally. “We are delighted to welcome Martin to the NovaBridge Board,” said Fu Wei, Chairman of the Board of NovaBridge. “Martin brings a rare combination of global healthcare experience, strategic insight, and governance expertise gained over decades of working with leading healthcare organizations around the world. As NovaBridge continues to grow and evolve, his perspective on board oversight, organizational development, and long-term value creation will be a valuable addition to our Board.” “I am honored to join NovaBridge at this important stage. I look forward to supporting the Board and management team with an independent perspective on strategy, governance, and long-term value creation,” said Mr. Dewhurst. The appointment follows the departure of independent director Liu Xin from the Board. The Company thanks Ms. Liu for her dedicated service and valuable contributions to NovaBridge. About Martin Dewhurst Martin Dewhurst has over 30 years of experience across biotech, biopharma, medical devices, health tech, and healthcare investment. Previously, he spent more than three decades at McKinsey & Company, where he co-led McKinsey’s Global Life Sciences Practice for seven years, doubling its scale and impact while innovating client services in digital and analytics. He also co-founded and co-led the McKinsey Health Institute, and led McKinsey’s Organization Practice in EMEA, with a focus on human capital, transformation, and post-merger integration. Earlier in his career, he worked with Arthur Andersen & Co. and BP Solar International.​ Mr. Dewhurst currently serves on the boards of Swixx BioPharma AG, Turn Therapeutics Inc. (Nasdaq: TTRX), Unilabs SA, Cytovation ASA, and Distalmotion SA, where he chairs the Audit Committee. He is also a member of the Remuneration Committee at Cytovation ASA. Previously, he served as Chair of the Advisory Board of MedGenome Labs Ltd. Mr. Dewhurst also serves as a Senior Advisor to Revival Healthcare Capital, PJT Partners’ Life Sciences practice, and Lightrock. Mr. Dewhurst received an M.B.A. from INSEAD, where he was named to the Dean’s List, and a B.A. from Magdalen College, Oxford. About NovaBridge NovaBridge Biosciences (Nasdaq: NBP) is a global biotechnology company advancing a portfolio of therapeutic programs in oncology and ophthalmology. The Company identifies differentiated therapeutic opportunities, generates value-defining clinical evidence, and applies the development, financing, and partnering strategy best suited to each program. NovaBridge’s portfolio is led by givastomig and VIS-101. The Company's objective is to build a sustainable biotechnology company by repeatedly identifying differentiated innovation, advancing it efficiently, and bringing novel therapies to patients through the path best suited to each opportunity. Martin Dewhurst has over 30 years of experience across biotech, biopharma, medical devices, health tech, and healthcare investment. Previously, he spent more than three decades at McKinsey & Company, where he co-led McKinsey’s Global Life Sciences Practice for seven years, doubling its scale and impact while innovating client services in digital and analytics. He also co-founded and co-led the McKinsey Health Institute, and led McKinsey’s Organization Practice in EMEA, with a focus on human capital, transformation, and post-merger integration. Earlier in his career, he worked with Arthur Andersen & Co. and BP Solar International.​
Mr. Dewhurst currently serves on the boards of Swixx BioPharma AG, Turn Therapeutics Inc. (Nasdaq: TTRX), Unilabs SA, Cytovation ASA, and Distalmotion SA, where he chairs the Audit Committee. He is also a member of the Remuneration Committee at Cytovation ASA. Previously, he served as Chair of the Advisory Board of MedGenome Labs Ltd. Mr. Dewhurst also serves as a Senior Advisor to Revival Healthcare Capital, PJT Partners’ Life Sciences practice, and Lightrock.
Mr. Dewhurst received an M.B.A. from INSEAD, where he was named to the Dean’s List, and a B.A. from Magdalen College, Oxford.
About NovaBridge
NovaBridge Biosciences (Nasdaq: NBP) is a global biotechnology company advancing a portfolio of therapeutic programs in oncology and ophthalmology. The Company identifies differentiated therapeutic opportunities, generates value-defining clinical evidence, and applies the development, financing, and partnering strategy best suited to each program.
NovaBridge’s portfolio is led by givastomig and VIS-101. The Company's objective is to build a sustainable biotechnology company by repeatedly identifying differentiated innovation, advancing it efficiently, and bringing novel therapies to patients through the path best suited to each opportunity.
For more information, please visit www.novabridge.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

To read more about the future of the RNA therapeutics market, get a snapshot @ https://www.delveinsight.com/report-store/rna-therapeutics-market Key Factors Contributing to the Rise in Growth of the RNA Therapeutics Market Growing Adoption of mRNA-Based Therapies: The successful development and commercialization of mRNA vaccines have demonstrated the therapeutic potential of RNA technologies. This has encouraged pharmaceutical companies to expand mRNA research into oncology, infectious diseases, rare disorders, and other therapeutic areas. Rising Prevalence of Chronic and Genetic Diseases: T he increasing burden of cancer, cardiovascular disorders, metabolic diseases, and rare genetic conditions is driving demand for innovative treatment approaches. RNA therapeutics can target disease pathways at the genetic or molecular level, creating opportunities for conditions with limited treatment options. Advancements in RNA Delivery Technologies: Improvements in lipid nanoparticles, conjugated delivery systems, and other RNA delivery platforms are enhancing the stability, cellular uptake, and targeted delivery of RNA molecules. These advances are helping overcome major limitations associated with earlier RNA-based approaches. Expansion of the RNA Therapeutics Pipeline: Pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies are rapidly expanding pipelines involving mRNA, small interfering RNA (siRNA), antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), and other RNA modalities. Increasing clinical-stage activity is broadening the potential applications of RNA therapeutics across multiple disease areas. Increasing Investment in RNA Research and Development: Venture capital, pharmaceutical partnerships, government funding, and strategic investments are supporting the development of RNA platforms and manufacturing capabilities. Rising investment is accelerating discovery programs, clinical development, and commercialization efforts. Growing Applications in Oncology: RNA technologies are increasingly being investigated for cancer vaccines, immune modulation, gene silencing, and personalized therapies. The ability to design RNA molecules against specific molecular targets is creating opportunities for precision oncology and individualized treatment approaches. Advances in RNA Manufacturing and Production: Improvements in large-scale RNA synthesis, purification, formulation, and quality-control processes are supporting the transition of RNA candidates from research to commercial production. More efficient manufacturing is also helping improve scalability and reduce production-related challenges. Increasing Use of Personalized Medicine: RNA therapeutics can be designed or modified according to specific genetic and molecular characteristics of diseases. This compatibility with precision medicine is encouraging their development for patient-specific therapies, particularly in oncology and genetic disorders. Supportive Regulatory Environment: Regulatory approvals of innovative RNA-based products have provided greater validation of the technology and encouraged further development. Regulatory pathways and incentives for rare diseases and breakthrough therapies are also supporting investment in novel RNA platforms. Strategic Partnerships and Licensing Activities: Collaborations between biotechnology companies, pharmaceutical firms, academic institutions, and technology providers are facilitating access to RNA platforms, delivery technologies, and manufacturing capabilities. Such partnerships are helping accelerate clinical development and commercial expansion. Growing Interest in Rare and Genetic Diseases: RNA-based approaches can modulate gene expression or address disease-causing genetic mechanisms, making them attractive for rare and inherited disorders. Increasing investment in these areas is expanding the addressable market for RNA therapeutics. Get a sneak peek at the RNA therapeutics market dynamics @ RNA Therapeutics Market Trends Regional RNA Therapeutics Market Insights North America North America held the largest share of the RNA therapeutics market, accounting for approximately 45% of the global market in 2025. The region’s leading position is attributed to its well-developed biopharmaceutical ecosystem, substantial R&D investments, and rapid adoption of advanced genetic medicine technologies. The presence of major pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, established regulatory frameworks, and early availability of innovative therapies further drives market expansion. Moreover, rising government support for biomedical research and robust clinical trial activity in the United States and Canada are expected to strengthen North America’s leadership in RNA-based drug development and commercialization. Europe The RNA therapeutics market in Europe is experiencing robust and sustained growth, supported by increasing regulatory backing from the European Medicines Agency (EMA), the rapid expansion of mRNA-based infectious disease programs, and growing late-stage clinical development activity across respiratory and viral diseases. The region has built a strong foundation for RNA therapeutics through earlier approvals of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, including Moderna’s Spikevax, which received EMA authorization in January 2021 and marked a significant milestone in the large-scale adoption of RNA technologies across Europe. Since then, the region has continued to expand its RNA therapeutic landscape through updated vaccines, new indications, and next-generation platforms. In July 2025, for instance, the EMA recommended an updated authorization for Moderna’s Spikevax targeting the LP.8.1 COVID-19 variant for the 2025–2026 vaccination season, demonstrating continued regulatory support for advancing mRNA vaccine technologies. More recently, in February 2026, the EMA recommended approval of Moderna’s combined COVID-19 and influenza mRNA vaccine, mCombriax, for adults aged 50 years and older, highlighting growing momentum toward combination RNA-based immunization approaches. In parallel with commercial developments, Europe is witnessing significant clinical research activity involving RNA-based therapies and vaccines for infectious and respiratory diseases. Moderna continues to advance late-stage clinical programs, including Phase 3 studies of its seasonal influenza mRNA vaccine candidate, mRNA-1010, as well as combination respiratory vaccines, with clinical trials being conducted at European sites during 2025–2026. GSK plc has also progressed its mRNA-based influenza vaccine candidate into late-stage development following encouraging mid-stage results that demonstrated strong immune responses among both younger and older adults, further strengthening Europe’s position in next-generation vaccine innovation. Meanwhile, companies such as Arcturus Therapeutics, Inc. are broadening RNA research in the region through self-amplifying mRNA vaccine platforms, including pandemic influenza (H5N1) candidates that entered Phase 1 development in 2025. Overall, strong regulatory support, the growing number of approvals for updated and combination mRNA vaccines, and an expanding clinical development pipeline are collectively driving the growth of Europe’s RNA therapeutics market. These factors are reinforcing the region’s role as a key and rapidly expanding market for next-generation RNA-based therapeutic and vaccine technologies. Asia-Pacific The Asia Pacific region is emerging as a key growth engine for the RNA therapeutics market, supported by strong government backing, expanding biotechnology infrastructure, large patient populations, and a rapidly growing clinical trial landscape. Countries including China, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and India are making substantial investments in mRNA, siRNA, and antisense RNA technologies to strengthen domestic biopharmaceutical capabilities and enhance pandemic preparedness. The region also benefits from cost-effective manufacturing capabilities, a well-established contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) ecosystem, and increasing collaborations between multinational pharmaceutical companies and local biotechnology firms. These factors are accelerating the development and commercialization of RNA-based therapies. Recent market insights indicate that APAC represents the fastest-growing regional market for RNA therapeutics, with growth particularly supported by infectious disease applications and government-funded research programs focused on nucleic acid medicines, especially in China and Japan. The region is also experiencing a notable increase in clinical trial activity across oncology, infectious diseases, and rare genetic disorders, further reinforcing its expanding role in the global RNA therapeutics landscape. In China, several mRNA-based clinical trials have received approval, including investigational RNA-based cancer therapies such as CSPC Pharmaceutical Group’s SYS6020, which entered human trials in 2024 for oncology and autoimmune applications. This development reflects the growing regulatory acceptance and clinical application of RNA technology platforms. Meanwhile, Japan is progressing multiple next-generation RNA and gene therapy programs through robust academic–industry partnerships and government-supported biotechnology initiatives centered on personalized medicine and regenerative therapies. India is likewise establishing itself as an important hub for vaccine research and development and large-scale manufacturing, supported by its expanding biotechnology industry and growing network of contract research organizations. To know more about why North America is leading the market growth in the RNA therapeutics market, get a snapshot of the RNA Therapeutics Market Analysis Recent Developmental Activities in the RNA Therapeutics Market In September 2026, UTR Therapeutics Inc. , a biotechnology company developing clinical trial-ready RNA therapeutics aimed at targeting previously undruggable proteins, announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) to 3′UTRMYCN M1-14 (UTRxMYCN M1-14) for the treatment of soft tissue sarcoma, including rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS). The FDA also granted Rare Pediatric Disease Designation (RPDD) to the therapy for the treatment of rhabdomyosarcoma. In September 2026, 4BIO Capital announced that it led a EUR 40 million seed financing round for Aptadir Therapeutics (Aptadir). The financing will support the advancement of Aptadir’s pipeline of disease-modifying investigational RNA therapeutics, including its lead program, CAP1-FMR1, which is being developed for the treatment of Fragile X Syndrome. Aptadir’s proprietary technology is built on the discovery of a novel class of RNAs capable of selectively preventing aberrant DNA methylation at the level of individual genes. In September 2026, Arcturus Therapeutics Holdings Inc. reported encouraging interim Phase 2 results for ARCT-810 in patients with ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency. The company also unveiled LUNAR 2.0™, its next-generation mRNA delivery platform, along with additional liver-focused pipeline programs. In August 2026, Rznomics Inc. announced that it will join Lilly Gateway Labs (LGL) in San Diego, California. In August 2026, Amplitude Therapeutics announced a strategic research collaboration and licensing agreement with Eli Lilly and Company to advance the discovery and development of taRNA-based vaccine candidates for infectious diseases. The initial collaboration will target undisclosed infectious disease vaccine programs addressing areas of significant unmet need, while Lilly will have the option to expand the partnership to include up to two additional infectious disease targets. In July 2026, miRecule, Inc. announced a strategic research collaboration with Rio Biofarma Brasil Ltda., a subsidiary of EMS S.A., Brazil’s largest pharmaceutical company. The collaboration aims to advance the co-development of peptide-mediated delivery technologies designed to enhance the targeted delivery of RNA therapeutics to extra-hepatic tissues, with potential applications across a broad spectrum of disease areas. In May 2026, EnPlusOne Biosciences, Inc. , a biotechnology company focused on advancing enzymatic technologies for RNA therapeutic discovery and development, announced plans to showcase new research findings and recent advances in enzymatic RNA synthesis at two major industry conferences in Boston during the month. What are RNA Therapeutics? RNA therapeutics are a class of medicines that use ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules to regulate gene expression, produce therapeutic proteins, or silence disease-causing genes. Unlike conventional drugs that primarily target proteins or cellular pathways, RNA-based therapies can act at the genetic and molecular level, offering a broader approach to treating diseases with previously difficult-to-drug targets. Major types include messenger RNA (mRNA), small interfering RNA (siRNA), antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), microRNA-based therapies, and RNA aptamers. mRNA therapeutics provide cells with instructions to produce specific proteins, while siRNA and ASOs can reduce or modify the expression of selected genes. Advances in RNA sequence design, chemical modification, and delivery technologies such as lipid nanoparticles and conjugated delivery systems have improved the stability, specificity, and therapeutic potential of these medicines. RNA therapeutics are being investigated and developed across a wide range of indications, including genetic disorders, cancer, cardiovascular diseases, infectious diseases, metabolic conditions, and neurological disorders, making them an increasingly important area of modern drug development. What are RNA Therapeutics? RNA therapeutics are a class of medicines that use ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules to regulate gene expression, produce therapeutic proteins, or silence disease-causing genes. Unlike conventional drugs that primarily target proteins or cellular pathways, RNA-based therapies can act at the genetic and molecular level, offering a broader approach to treating diseases with previously difficult-to-drug targets. Major types include messenger RNA (mRNA), small interfering RNA (siRNA), antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), microRNA-based therapies, and RNA aptamers. mRNA therapeutics provide cells with instructions to produce specific proteins, while siRNA and ASOs can reduce or modify the expression of selected genes. Advances in RNA sequence design, chemical modification, and delivery technologies such as lipid nanoparticles and conjugated delivery systems have improved the stability, specificity, and therapeutic potential of these medicines. RNA therapeutics are being investigated and developed across a wide range of indications, including genetic disorders, cancer, cardiovascular diseases, infectious diseases, metabolic conditions, and neurological disorders, making them an increasingly important area of modern drug development. Europe
The RNA therapeutics market in Europe is experiencing robust and sustained growth, supported by increasing regulatory backing from the European Medicines Agency (EMA), the rapid expansion of mRNA-based infectious disease programs, and growing late-stage clinical development activity across respiratory and viral diseases. The region has built a strong foundation for RNA therapeutics through earlier approvals of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, including Moderna’s Spikevax, which received EMA authorization in January 2021 and marked a significant milestone in the large-scale adoption of RNA technologies across Europe. Since then, the region has continued to expand its RNA therapeutic landscape through updated vaccines, new indications, and next-generation platforms. In July 2025, for instance, the EMA recommended an updated authorization for Moderna’s Spikevax targeting the LP.8.1 COVID-19 variant for the 2025–2026 vaccination season, demonstrating continued regulatory support for advancing mRNA vaccine technologies. More recently, in February 2026, the EMA recommended approval of Moderna’s combined COVID-19 and influenza mRNA vaccine, mCombriax, for adults aged 50 years and older, highlighting growing momentum toward combination RNA-based immunization approaches. In parallel with commercial developments, Europe is witnessing significant clinical research activity involving RNA-based therapies and vaccines for infectious and respiratory diseases. Moderna continues to advance late-stage clinical programs, including Phase 3 studies of its seasonal influenza mRNA vaccine candidate, mRNA-1010, as well as combination respiratory vaccines, with clinical trials being conducted at European sites during 2025–2026. GSK plc has also progressed its mRNA-based influenza vaccine candidate into late-stage development following encouraging mid-stage results that demonstrated strong immune responses among both younger and older adults, further strengthening Europe’s position in next-generation vaccine innovation. Meanwhile, companies such as Arcturus Therapeutics, Inc. are broadening RNA research in the region through self-amplifying mRNA vaccine platforms, including pandemic influenza (H5N1) candidates that entered Phase 1 development in 2025. Overall, strong regulatory support, the growing number of approvals for updated and combination mRNA vaccines, and an expanding clinical development pipeline are collectively driving the growth of Europe’s RNA therapeutics market. These factors are reinforcing the region’s role as a key and rapidly expanding market for next-generation RNA-based therapeutic and vaccine technologies.

What are RNA Therapeutics?
RNA therapeutics are a class of medicines that use ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules to regulate gene expression, produce therapeutic proteins, or silence disease-causing genes. Unlike conventional drugs that primarily target proteins or cellular pathways, RNA-based therapies can act at the genetic and molecular level, offering a broader approach to treating diseases with previously difficult-to-drug targets. Major types include messenger RNA (mRNA), small interfering RNA (siRNA), antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), microRNA-based therapies, and RNA aptamers. mRNA therapeutics provide cells with instructions to produce specific proteins, while siRNA and ASOs can reduce or modify the expression of selected genes. Advances in RNA sequence design, chemical modification, and delivery technologies such as lipid nanoparticles and conjugated delivery systems have improved the stability, specificity, and therapeutic potential of these medicines. RNA therapeutics are being investigated and developed across a wide range of indications, including genetic disorders, cancer, cardiovascular diseases, infectious diseases, metabolic conditions, and neurological disorders, making them an increasingly important area of modern drug development.

Accessibility: Skip TopNav Genmab and AbbVie Announce Epcoritamab in Combination with R-CHOP Demonstrates Statistically Significant Improvement in Progression-Free Survival in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma October 05, 2026 14:49 ET | Source: Genmab A/S Genmab A/S Company Announcement COPENHAGEN, Denmark and NORTH CHICAGO, Ill.; October 5, 2026 EPCORE DLBCL-2 is the first Phase 3 study of a bispecific antibody combination therapy to demonstrate statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in frontline diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) patients Based on the topline results, Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) and AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) announced today positive topline results from the Phase 3 EPCORE DLBCL-2 trial evaluating fixed treatment duration epcoritamab, a T-cell engaging bispecific antibody administered subcutaneously , in combination with standard of care rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin hydrochloride, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP), compared to R-CHOP alone, in newly diagnosed patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2 to 5. The trial demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in DLBCL patients with an IPI score of 2 to 5. The risk of disease progression or death was reduced by 51% (HR 0.49 [95% CI 0.36, 0.67]; p-value < 0.0001). The safety profile of epcoritamab when administered in combination with standard of care R-CHOP was generally well tolerated and consistent with the previously reported safety profiles of the individual agents (epcoritamab and R-CHOP). “These topline results of epcoritamab in combination with R-CHOP mark the first Phase 3 study to demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival in patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL treated with a bispecific antibody combination and have the potential to reshape the frontline treatment landscape,” said Jan van de Winkel, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Genmab. “While treatment advances have improved outcomes for patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, options for newly diagnosed patients remain limited, reinforcing the need for additional therapies that can treat as many patients as possible in the frontline setting.” “DLBCL is an aggressive disease and the need to advance treatment options is critical. These positive topline results suggest that epcoritamab combined with R-CHOP could offer a potential new standard of care in newly diagnosed DLBCL patients,” said Daejin Abidoye, MD, vice president, therapeutic area head, oncology, solid tumor and hematology, AbbVie. “The findings further strengthen our understanding and potential of bispecifics across the lymphoma treatment landscape, as we work to address urgent needs in this patient population.” "As an investigator with firsthand experience in both the landmark trial that established R-CHOP as a standard of care nearly 25 years ago and EPCORE DLBCL-2, it is particularly meaningful to see the potential benefit of bispecific antibody therapy in newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma,” said Gilles Salles, MD, PhD, Chief of the Lymphoma Service and holder of the Steven A. Greenberg Chair at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. “The 51% reduction in the risk of progression or death is clinically meaningful and highly relevant to everyday practice. These results have the potential to be practice-changing and could mark an important step forward in bringing the opportunity of cure to more patients.” Data will be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting. Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities to determine next steps. Epcoritamab plus R-CHOP is an investigational combination not approved by regulatory authorities. About the EPCORE ® DLBCL-2 Trial EPCORE DLBCL-2 ( NCT05578976 ) is a global Phase 3 open label, multi-center, randomized trial to evaluate the efficacy of fixed duration, subcutaneous epcoritamab (GEN3013, DuoBody ® -CD3xCD20) and standard of care rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin hydrochloride, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP) compared to R-CHOP alone in patients with newly diagnosed large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). The trial enrolled subjects with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2 to 5, including patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS), high-grade B-Cell lymphoma (HGBL) with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements, follicular lymphoma grade 3B (FL3B), T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-Cell lymphoma (TCHR LBLC), and Epstein-Barr Virus-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (EBV+ DLBCL). The primary endpoint is PFS in participants with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) of 3-5 and the key secondary endpoint is PFS in total participants (IPI score of 2-5). The risk of disease progression or death for the primary endpoint population was reduced by 51% (HR 0.49 [95% CI 0.35, 0.69]; p-value < 0.0001). Patients were randomized 2:1 to receive a fixed-duration regimen of epcoritamab plus R-CHOP for six cycles followed by epcoritamab alone for two cycles, or R-CHOP for six cycles followed by rituximab for two cycles. The trial started on February 8, 2023, and is ongoing. More information on this trial can be found at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05578976 (NCT: NCT05578976). About Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) DLBCL is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) worldwide, accounting for approximately 25-30 percent of all NHL cases. i , ii In the U.S., there are approximately 25,000 new cases of DLBCL diagnosed each year. iii DLBCL can arise in lymph nodes as well as in organs outside of the lymphatic system, occurs more commonly in the elderly and is slightly more prevalent in men. iv , v DLBCL is a fast-growing type of NHL, a cancer that develops in the lymphatic system and affects B-cell lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell. For many people living with DLBCL, their cancer either relapses, which means it may return after treatment, or becomes refractory, meaning it does not respond to treatment. Although new therapies have become available, treatment management can remain a challenge. iv , vi About Epcoritamab Epcoritamab is an IgG1-bispecific antibody created using Genmab's proprietary DuoBody technology and administered subcutaneously. Genmab's DuoBody-CD3 technology is designed to direct cytotoxic T cells selectively to elicit an immune response toward target cell types. Epcoritamab is designed to simultaneously bind to CD3 on T cells and CD20 on B cells and induces T-cell-mediated killing of CD20+ cells. vii Epcoritamab (approved under the brand name EPKINLY ® in the U.S. and Japan, and TEPKINLY ® in the EU) has received regulatory approval in certain lymphoma indications in more than 65 countries. Where approved, epcoritamab is a readily accessible therapy. Epcoritamab is being co-developed by Genmab and AbbVie as part of the companies' oncology collaboration. The companies share commercial responsibilities in the U.S. and Japan, with AbbVie responsible for further global commercialization. Both companies will pursue additional international regulatory approvals for the relapsed or refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL) indication and additional approvals for the R/R diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) indication. Genmab and AbbVie continue to evaluate the use of epcoritamab as a monotherapy, and in combination, across lines of therapy in a range of hematologic malignancies. This includes a trial evaluating epcoritamab in combination with lenalidomide and rituximab (R 2 ) compared to chemoimmunotherapy in patients with previously untreated FL ( NCT06191744 ). The safety and efficacy of epcoritamab has not been established for these investigational uses. Please visit www.clinicaltrials.gov for more information. About Genmab Genmab is an international biotechnology company dedicated to improving the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases through innovative antibody medicines. For over 25 years, its passionate, innovative and collaborative team has advanced a broad range of antibody-based therapeutic formats, including bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), immune-modulating antibodies and other next-generation modalities. Genmab’s science powers eight approved antibody medicines, and the company is advancing a strong late-stage clinical pipeline, including wholly owned programs, with the goal of delivering transformative medicines to patients. Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com or follow us on LinkedIn , X , Facebook and Instagram . About AbbVie in Oncology AbbVie is committed to elevating standards of care and bringing transformative therapies to patients worldwide living with difficult-to-treat cancers. We are advancing a dynamic pipeline of investigational therapies across a range of cancer types in both blood cancers and solid tumors. We are focusing on creating targeted medicines that either impede the reproduction of cancer cells or enable their elimination. We achieve this through various, targeted treatment modalities and biology interventions, including small molecule therapeutics, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), immuno-oncology-based therapeutics, multispecific antibody and novel CAR-T platforms. Our dedicated and experienced team joins forces with innovative partners to accelerate the delivery of potential breakthrough medicines. Today, our expansive oncology portfolio is comprised of approved and investigational treatments for a wide range of blood and solid tumors. We are evaluating more than 35 investigational medicines across some of the world's most widespread and debilitating cancers. As we work to have a remarkable impact on people's lives, we are committed to exploring solutions to help patients obtain access to our cancer medicines. For more information, please visit us at http://www.abbvie.com/oncology . About AbbVie AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, neuroscience and oncology – and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook , Instagram , X and YouTube. Genmab and AbbVie Announce Epcoritamab in Combination with R-CHOP Demonstrates Statistically Significant Improvement in Progression-Free Survival in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma October 05, 2026 14:49 ET | Source: Genmab A/S Genmab A/S Company Announcement COPENHAGEN, Denmark and NORTH CHICAGO, Ill.; October 5, 2026 EPCORE DLBCL-2 is the first Phase 3 study of a bispecific antibody combination therapy to demonstrate statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in frontline diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) patients Based on the topline results, Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) and AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) announced today positive topline results from the Phase 3 EPCORE DLBCL-2 trial evaluating fixed treatment duration epcoritamab, a T-cell engaging bispecific antibody administered subcutaneously , in combination with standard of care rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin hydrochloride, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP), compared to R-CHOP alone, in newly diagnosed patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2 to 5. The trial demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in DLBCL patients with an IPI score of 2 to 5. The risk of disease progression or death was reduced by 51% (HR 0.49 [95% CI 0.36, 0.67]; p-value < 0.0001). The safety profile of epcoritamab when administered in combination with standard of care R-CHOP was generally well tolerated and consistent with the previously reported safety profiles of the individual agents (epcoritamab and R-CHOP). “These topline results of epcoritamab in combination with R-CHOP mark the first Phase 3 study to demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival in patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL treated with a bispecific antibody combination and have the potential to reshape the frontline treatment landscape,” said Jan van de Winkel, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Genmab. “While treatment advances have improved outcomes for patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, options for newly diagnosed patients remain limited, reinforcing the need for additional therapies that can treat as many patients as possible in the frontline setting.” “DLBCL is an aggressive disease and the need to advance treatment options is critical. These positive topline results suggest that epcoritamab combined with R-CHOP could offer a potential new standard of care in newly diagnosed DLBCL patients,” said Daejin Abidoye, MD, vice president, therapeutic area head, oncology, solid tumor and hematology, AbbVie. “The findings further strengthen our understanding and potential of bispecifics across the lymphoma treatment landscape, as we work to address urgent needs in this patient population.” "As an investigator with firsthand experience in both the landmark trial that established R-CHOP as a standard of care nearly 25 years ago and EPCORE DLBCL-2, it is particularly meaningful to see the potential benefit of bispecific antibody therapy in newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma,” said Gilles Salles, MD, PhD, Chief of the Lymphoma Service and holder of the Steven A. Greenberg Chair at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. “The 51% reduction in the risk of progression or death is clinically meaningful and highly relevant to everyday practice. These results have the potential to be practice-changing and could mark an important step forward in bringing the opportunity of cure to more patients.” Data will be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting. Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities to determine next steps. Epcoritamab plus R-CHOP is an investigational combination not approved by regulatory authorities. About the EPCORE ® DLBCL-2 Trial EPCORE DLBCL-2 ( NCT05578976 ) is a global Phase 3 open label, multi-center, randomized trial to evaluate the efficacy of fixed duration, subcutaneous epcoritamab (GEN3013, DuoBody ® -CD3xCD20) and standard of care rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin hydrochloride, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP) compared to R-CHOP alone in patients with newly diagnosed large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). The trial enrolled subjects with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2 to 5, including patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS), high-grade B-Cell lymphoma (HGBL) with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements, follicular lymphoma grade 3B (FL3B), T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-Cell lymphoma (TCHR LBLC), and Epstein-Barr Virus-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (EBV+ DLBCL). The primary endpoint is PFS in participants with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) of 3-5 and the key secondary endpoint is PFS in total participants (IPI score of 2-5). The risk of disease progression or death for the primary endpoint population was reduced by 51% (HR 0.49 [95% CI 0.35, 0.69]; p-value < 0.0001). Patients were randomized 2:1 to receive a fixed-duration regimen of epcoritamab plus R-CHOP for six cycles followed by epcoritamab alone for two cycles, or R-CHOP for six cycles followed by rituximab for two cycles. The trial started on February 8, 2023, and is ongoing. More information on this trial can be found at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05578976 (NCT: NCT05578976). About Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) DLBCL is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) worldwide, accounting for approximately 25-30 percent of all NHL cases. i , ii In the U.S., there are approximately 25,000 new cases of DLBCL diagnosed each year. iii DLBCL can arise in lymph nodes as well as in organs outside of the lymphatic system, occurs more commonly in the elderly and is slightly more prevalent in men. iv , v DLBCL is a fast-growing type of NHL, a cancer that develops in the lymphatic system and affects B-cell lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell. For many people living with DLBCL, their cancer either relapses, which means it may return after treatment, or becomes refractory, meaning it does not respond to treatment. Although new therapies have become available, treatment management can remain a challenge. iv , vi About Epcoritamab Epcoritamab is an IgG1-bispecific antibody created using Genmab's proprietary DuoBody technology and administered subcutaneously. Genmab's DuoBody-CD3 technology is designed to direct cytotoxic T cells selectively to elicit an immune response toward target cell types. Epcoritamab is designed to simultaneously bind to CD3 on T cells and CD20 on B cells and induces T-cell-mediated killing of CD20+ cells. vii Epcoritamab (approved under the brand name EPKINLY ® in the U.S. and Japan, and TEPKINLY ® in the EU) has received regulatory approval in certain lymphoma indications in more than 65 countries. Where approved, epcoritamab is a readily accessible therapy. Epcoritamab is being co-developed by Genmab and AbbVie as part of the companies' oncology collaboration. The companies share commercial responsibilities in the U.S. and Japan, with AbbVie responsible for further global commercialization. Both companies will pursue additional international regulatory approvals for the relapsed or refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL) indication and additional approvals for the R/R diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) indication. Genmab and AbbVie continue to evaluate the use of epcoritamab as a monotherapy, and in combination, across lines of therapy in a range of hematologic malignancies. This includes a trial evaluating epcoritamab in combination with lenalidomide and rituximab (R 2 ) compared to chemoimmunotherapy in patients with previously untreated FL ( NCT06191744 ). The safety and efficacy of epcoritamab has not been established for these investigational uses. Please visit www.clinicaltrials.gov for more information. Company Announcement COPENHAGEN, Denmark and NORTH CHICAGO, Ill.; October 5, 2026 EPCORE DLBCL-2 is the first Phase 3 study of a bispecific antibody combination therapy to demonstrate statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in frontline diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) patients Based on the topline results, Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) and AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) announced today positive topline results from the Phase 3 EPCORE DLBCL-2 trial evaluating fixed treatment duration epcoritamab, a T-cell engaging bispecific antibody administered subcutaneously , in combination with standard of care rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin hydrochloride, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP), compared to R-CHOP alone, in newly diagnosed patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2 to 5. The trial demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in DLBCL patients with an IPI score of 2 to 5. The risk of disease progression or death was reduced by 51% (HR 0.49 [95% CI 0.36, 0.67]; p-value < 0.0001). The safety profile of epcoritamab when administered in combination with standard of care R-CHOP was generally well tolerated and consistent with the previously reported safety profiles of the individual agents (epcoritamab and R-CHOP). “These topline results of epcoritamab in combination with R-CHOP mark the first Phase 3 study to demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival in patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL treated with a bispecific antibody combination and have the potential to reshape the frontline treatment landscape,” said Jan van de Winkel, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Genmab. “While treatment advances have improved outcomes for patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, options for newly diagnosed patients remain limited, reinforcing the need for additional therapies that can treat as many patients as possible in the frontline setting.” “DLBCL is an aggressive disease and the need to advance treatment options is critical. These positive topline results suggest that epcoritamab combined with R-CHOP could offer a potential new standard of care in newly diagnosed DLBCL patients,” said Daejin Abidoye, MD, vice president, therapeutic area head, oncology, solid tumor and hematology, AbbVie. “The findings further strengthen our understanding and potential of bispecifics across the lymphoma treatment landscape, as we work to address urgent needs in this patient population.” "As an investigator with firsthand experience in both the landmark trial that established R-CHOP as a standard of care nearly 25 years ago and EPCORE DLBCL-2, it is particularly meaningful to see the potential benefit of bispecific antibody therapy in newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma,” said Gilles Salles, MD, PhD, Chief of the Lymphoma Service and holder of the Steven A. Greenberg Chair at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. “The 51% reduction in the risk of progression or death is clinically meaningful and highly relevant to everyday practice. These results have the potential to be practice-changing and could mark an important step forward in bringing the opportunity of cure to more patients.” Data will be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting. Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities to determine next steps. Epcoritamab plus R-CHOP is an investigational combination not approved by regulatory authorities. About the EPCORE ® DLBCL-2 Trial EPCORE DLBCL-2 ( NCT05578976 ) is a global Phase 3 open label, multi-center, randomized trial to evaluate the efficacy of fixed duration, subcutaneous epcoritamab (GEN3013, DuoBody ® -CD3xCD20) and standard of care rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin hydrochloride, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP) compared to R-CHOP alone in patients with newly diagnosed large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). The trial enrolled subjects with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2 to 5, including patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS), high-grade B-Cell lymphoma (HGBL) with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements, follicular lymphoma grade 3B (FL3B), T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-Cell lymphoma (TCHR LBLC), and Epstein-Barr Virus-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (EBV+ DLBCL). The primary endpoint is PFS in participants with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) of 3-5 and the key secondary endpoint is PFS in total participants (IPI score of 2-5). The risk of disease progression or death for the primary endpoint population was reduced by 51% (HR 0.49 [95% CI 0.35, 0.69]; p-value < 0.0001). Patients were randomized 2:1 to receive a fixed-duration regimen of epcoritamab plus R-CHOP for six cycles followed by epcoritamab alone for two cycles, or R-CHOP for six cycles followed by rituximab for two cycles. The trial started on February 8, 2023, and is ongoing. More information on this trial can be found at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05578976 (NCT: NCT05578976). About Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) DLBCL is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) worldwide, accounting for approximately 25-30 percent of all NHL cases. i , ii In the U.S., there are approximately 25,000 new cases of DLBCL diagnosed each year. iii DLBCL can arise in lymph nodes as well as in organs outside of the lymphatic system, occurs more commonly in the elderly and is slightly more prevalent in men. iv , v DLBCL is a fast-growing type of NHL, a cancer that develops in the lymphatic system and affects B-cell lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell. For many people living with DLBCL, their cancer either relapses, which means it may return after treatment, or becomes refractory, meaning it does not respond to treatment. Although new therapies have become available, treatment management can remain a challenge. iv , vi About Epcoritamab Epcoritamab is an IgG1-bispecific antibody created using Genmab's proprietary DuoBody technology and administered subcutaneously. Genmab's DuoBody-CD3 technology is designed to direct cytotoxic T cells selectively to elicit an immune response toward target cell types. Epcoritamab is designed to simultaneously bind to CD3 on T cells and CD20 on B cells and induces T-cell-mediated killing of CD20+ cells. vii Epcoritamab (approved under the brand name EPKINLY ® in the U.S. and Japan, and TEPKINLY ® in the EU) has received regulatory approval in certain lymphoma indications in more than 65 countries. Where approved, epcoritamab is a readily accessible therapy. Epcoritamab is being co-developed by Genmab and AbbVie as part of the companies' oncology collaboration. The companies share commercial responsibilities in the U.S. and Japan, with AbbVie responsible for further global commercialization. Both companies will pursue additional international regulatory approvals for the relapsed or refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL) indication and additional approvals for the R/R diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) indication. Genmab and AbbVie continue to evaluate the use of epcoritamab as a monotherapy, and in combination, across lines of therapy in a range of hematologic malignancies. This includes a trial evaluating epcoritamab in combination with lenalidomide and rituximab (R 2 ) compared to chemoimmunotherapy in patients with previously untreated FL ( NCT06191744 ). The safety and efficacy of epcoritamab has not been established for these investigational uses. Please visit www.clinicaltrials.gov for more information. EPCORE DLBCL-2 is the first Phase 3 study of a bispecific antibody combination therapy to demonstrate statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in frontline diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) patients Based on the topline results, Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities
EPCORE DLBCL-2 is the first Phase 3 study of a bispecific antibody combination therapy to demonstrate statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in frontline diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) patients
Based on the topline results, Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities
Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) and AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) announced today positive topline results from the Phase 3 EPCORE DLBCL-2 trial evaluating fixed treatment duration epcoritamab, a T-cell engaging bispecific antibody administered subcutaneously , in combination with standard of care rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin hydrochloride, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP), compared to R-CHOP alone, in newly diagnosed patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2 to 5. The trial demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) in DLBCL patients with an IPI score of 2 to 5. The risk of disease progression or death was reduced by 51% (HR 0.49 [95% CI 0.36, 0.67]; p-value < 0.0001). The safety profile of epcoritamab when administered in combination with standard of care R-CHOP was generally well tolerated and consistent with the previously reported safety profiles of the individual agents (epcoritamab and R-CHOP).

“These topline results of epcoritamab in combination with R-CHOP mark the first Phase 3 study to demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival in patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL treated with a bispecific antibody combination and have the potential to reshape the frontline treatment landscape,” said Jan van de Winkel, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Genmab. “While treatment advances have improved outcomes for patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, options for newly diagnosed patients remain limited, reinforcing the need for additional therapies that can treat as many patients as possible in the frontline setting.”
“DLBCL is an aggressive disease and the need to advance treatment options is critical. These positive topline results suggest that epcoritamab combined with R-CHOP could offer a potential new standard of care in newly diagnosed DLBCL patients,” said Daejin Abidoye, MD, vice president, therapeutic area head, oncology, solid tumor and hematology, AbbVie. “The findings further strengthen our understanding and potential of bispecifics across the lymphoma treatment landscape, as we work to address urgent needs in this patient population.”
"As an investigator with firsthand experience in both the landmark trial that established R-CHOP as a standard of care nearly 25 years ago and EPCORE DLBCL-2, it is particularly meaningful to see the potential benefit of bispecific antibody therapy in newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma,” said Gilles Salles, MD, PhD, Chief of the Lymphoma Service and holder of the Steven A. Greenberg Chair at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. “The 51% reduction in the risk of progression or death is clinically meaningful and highly relevant to everyday practice. These results have the potential to be practice-changing and could mark an important step forward in bringing the opportunity of cure to more patients.”
Data will be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting. Genmab and AbbVie will engage global regulatory authorities to determine next steps. Epcoritamab plus R-CHOP is an investigational combination not approved by regulatory authorities.
About the EPCORE ® DLBCL-2 Trial EPCORE DLBCL-2 ( NCT05578976 ) is a global Phase 3 open label, multi-center, randomized trial to evaluate the efficacy of fixed duration, subcutaneous epcoritamab (GEN3013, DuoBody ® -CD3xCD20) and standard of care rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin hydrochloride, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP) compared to R-CHOP alone in patients with newly diagnosed large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). The trial enrolled subjects with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2 to 5, including patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS), high-grade B-Cell lymphoma (HGBL) with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements, follicular lymphoma grade 3B (FL3B), T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-Cell lymphoma (TCHR LBLC), and Epstein-Barr Virus-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (EBV+ DLBCL). The primary endpoint is PFS in participants with an International Prognostic Index (IPI) of 3-5 and the key secondary endpoint is PFS in total participants (IPI score of 2-5). The risk of disease progression or death for the primary endpoint population was reduced by 51% (HR 0.49 [95% CI 0.35, 0.69]; p-value < 0.0001). Patients were randomized 2:1 to receive a fixed-duration regimen of epcoritamab plus R-CHOP for six cycles followed by epcoritamab alone for two cycles, or R-CHOP for six cycles followed by rituximab for two cycles. The trial started on February 8, 2023, and is ongoing.

About Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) DLBCL is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) worldwide, accounting for approximately 25-30 percent of all NHL cases. i , ii In the U.S., there are approximately 25,000 new cases of DLBCL diagnosed each year. iii DLBCL can arise in lymph nodes as well as in organs outside of the lymphatic system, occurs more commonly in the elderly and is slightly more prevalent in men. iv , v DLBCL is a fast-growing type of NHL, a cancer that develops in the lymphatic system and affects B-cell lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell. For many people living with DLBCL, their cancer either relapses, which means it may return after treatment, or becomes refractory, meaning it does not respond to treatment. Although new therapies have become available, treatment management can remain a challenge. iv , vi

About Epcoritamab Epcoritamab is an IgG1-bispecific antibody created using Genmab's proprietary DuoBody technology and administered subcutaneously. Genmab's DuoBody-CD3 technology is designed to direct cytotoxic T cells selectively to elicit an immune response toward target cell types. Epcoritamab is designed to simultaneously bind to CD3 on T cells and CD20 on B cells and induces T-cell-mediated killing of CD20+ cells. vii
About Epcoritamab
vii
Epcoritamab (approved under the brand name EPKINLY ® in the U.S. and Japan, and TEPKINLY ® in the EU) has received regulatory approval in certain lymphoma indications in more than 65 countries. Where approved, epcoritamab is a readily accessible therapy. Epcoritamab is being co-developed by Genmab and AbbVie as part of the companies' oncology collaboration. The companies share commercial responsibilities in the U.S. and Japan, with AbbVie responsible for further global commercialization. Both companies will pursue additional international regulatory approvals for the relapsed or refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL) indication and additional approvals for the R/R diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) indication.
Genmab and AbbVie continue to evaluate the use of epcoritamab as a monotherapy, and in combination, across lines of therapy in a range of hematologic malignancies. This includes a trial evaluating epcoritamab in combination with lenalidomide and rituximab (R 2 ) compared to chemoimmunotherapy in patients with previously untreated FL ( NCT06191744 ). The safety and efficacy of epcoritamab has not been established for these investigational uses. Please visit www.clinicaltrials.gov for more information.
